glance: 145 km to Narail by road, 4–5 hours by bus or car
sm-sultan-memorial.desc: S.M. Sultan (1923–1994) spent most of his life in Narail, painting farmers, fishermen and village women with huge, powerful bodies. His home at Machimdia on the Chitra is now a memorial with a gallery of his works, his grave and the big boat he built for children. The grounds are shaded and close to the water. It is the essential stop in Narail.
blocks: How to get there
A short rickshaw ride from Narail town to Machimdia on the riverbank.
Good to know
Check opening days locally; photography may be restricted inside the gallery.

glance: Village homes and winter fairs around Narail
narail-khejur-rosh.desc: When date palm juice is plentiful, families boil it with fragrant rice and milk until thick and caramel-coloured. The result tastes of smoke and fresh sap rather than plain sugar. It is cooked at home and sometimes served at winter gatherings. Ask a homestay or village host if you get the chance.
blocks: Good to know
Eat it cooked; avoid drinking raw date sap because of the Nipah virus risk.

glance: 145 km to Narail by road, 4–5 hours by bus or car
goal-bathan-mosque.desc: Goal Bathan Mosque is in Goalbathan village of Narail Sadar upazila. Banglapedia lists it, with the date 1654, as the upazila's one archaeological relic, while the local Islamic Foundation office calls it a Mughal-era building about 450 years old. Villagers tell the story that jinn built it overnight. It has been added to a government project for preserving old mosques, so it is worth seeing before repairs change it.
blocks: How to get there
From Narail town take an easy-bike or CNG north towards Goalbathan village.
Good to know
It is a working village mosque; visit outside prayer times and dress modestly.

chitra-boat-race-sultan-mela.desc: Narail hosts boat races on the Chitra with long, narrow boats driven by dozens of oarsmen singing to keep rhythm. The races are linked to the memory of S.M. Sultan, and crowds fill the banks, rooftops and even trees to watch. Around his birth anniversary the Sultan Mela brings art exhibitions, jari and kobi gaan, wrestling and lathi khela. Dates vary each year, so check locally.
blocks: Good to know
Arrive early for a good spot on the bank; the crowds are large.

glance: 145 km to Narail by road, 4–5 hours by bus or car
chitra-riverfront-narail.desc: The Chitra runs past Narail town, its banks lined with trees, small ghats and fishing boats. It inspired many of Sultan's landscapes and is the stage for the town's boat races. An evening ferry crossing or walk along the bank shows daily river life. In the monsoon it runs full; in winter it is clear and calm.
blocks: How to get there
Walk or take a rickshaw to the ferry ghat in Narail town.
Good to know
Hire a small boat for an hour at sunset; agree the price first.

glance: 145 km to Narail by road, 4–5 hours by bus or car
raigram-jor-bangla-temple.desc: This temple stands in Raigram village of Lohagara upazila, on the bank of the Nabaganga. It is built in the jor bangla style, two curved dochala huts joined side by side, like the temples raised under Raja Sitaram of Mohammadpur. Tradition says Ramshankar, younger brother of Sitaram's general Menahati, built it, and a Shiva temple beside it carries an inscription of about 1724. The Department of Archaeology lists it as a protected monument.
blocks: How to get there
Take a bus or CNG from Narail town to Lohagara, then an easy-bike to Raigram on the Nabaganga.
Good to know
If you have a car for the day, add Raja Sitaram's palace ruins at Mohammadpur in Magura, about 20 km to the north.

glance: 145 km to Narail by road, 4–5 hours by bus or car
narail-zamindar-bari.desc: The Narail zamindars built large houses, temples and tanks in the 19th century, and the town grew around their estate. Much of the complex is now in ruins, with trees growing from old brick walls. A few buildings and a large pond remain in use. Wandering through gives a sense of the town's colonial-era past.
blocks: How to get there
Within Narail town; any rickshaw puller knows the way.
Good to know
Parts are unsafe structurally; keep out of crumbling interiors.

glance: Winter patali haats around Narail and Kalia
narail-nalini-patali.desc: Narail is known for high-quality date palm molasses. The first sap of the season makes the most fragrant gur, and the best set cakes are sold as nolen patali. Winter haats here are lined with clay pots and stacked cakes. It is also used in sandesh and payesh.

glance: 145 km to Narail by road, 4–5 hours by bus or car
nihar-ranjan-gupta-house.desc: Nihar Ranjan Gupta, creator of the detective Kiriti Roy, came from a family based in Lohagara, Narail. Their ancestral house has been declared an archaeological monument. It is an old brick building in a rural setting, visited mostly by literature lovers. Few travellers make it here, so expect a quiet visit.
blocks: How to get there
Bus from Narail to Lohagara, then ask locals for the house.
Good to know
There are no facilities; respect the families living nearby.

glance: 145 km to Narail by road, 4–5 hours by bus or car
hatbaria-zamindar-bari.desc: Kali Shankar Roy, founder of the Narail zamindar line, split his estate between two sons: the elder kept the Narail house and the younger, Joy Narayan Roy, got Hatbaria. The Hatbaria house is now widely known after its last zamindar, Jitendranath Roy, whose family left for India before Partition. Most of the buildings have collapsed, but the zamindars' temple and a cement-finished bathing ghat on the Chitra, called Nam Ghat or Badha Ghat, still stand. The district administration has asked the Department of Archaeology to protect what remains, and work on a park on the grounds has been under way.
blocks: How to get there
It is in Narail Sadar near the town; take a rickshaw or easy-bike to Hatbaria on the Chitra bank.
Good to know
Late afternoon is best for the river from the ghat. Combine with the Narail Zamindar Bari and the S.M. Sultan complex the same day.
